These calculi have unique phase-affine normal forms, and the resulting equational theories are complete: semantic equality coincides with derivable equality.

Logic in Computer Science.title: How to prove equations using diagrams: A categorical and operational semantics for e-graphs
Logic in Computer Science.summary: E-graphs are a powerful algorithmic technique for automated equational reasoning but have resisted a conceptual understanding independent of issues of presentation and implementation. We propose an operational semantics for e-graphs based on the fundamental category-theoretic concepts of diagrams, limits, and initial functors. We illustrate the formalism through numerous example calculations and establish its soundness and completeness. Technical prerequisites are kept to a minimum in the main text; less standard elements of the mathematical theory are developed in two appendices.

Logic in Computer Science.title: The Scope Grammar of Natural-Language Rules: Counting and Enumerating Readings modulo Logical Equivalence
Logic in Computer Science.summary: A rule written for people fixes its atomic conditions and connectives but leaves open how the connectives are bracketed, and each bracketing is a different logical reading that an autoformalizer must resolve or expose. We study the scope grammar, a deliberately ambiguous context-free grammar whose derivation trees are the readings of a connective skeleton and whose quotient by logical equivalence is what matters downstream. A skeleton with $k$ binary connectives has $C_k$ derivation trees, the $k$-th Catalan number, but far fewer logically distinct readings. For the positive, repetition-free fragment we make the gap exact: through the uniqueness of the read-once normal form we characterize the realizable normal forms by lowest common ancestors and count them with a two-label recurrence over the operator word, verified against exhaustive enumeration up to eleven atoms. The count is invariant under reversal and $\wedge/\vee$ duality; a skeleton is ambiguous if and only if it uses both $\wedge$ and $\vee$, a one-pass test; and the number of classes is at least $2^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$. Up to fifteen atoms the alternating pattern is the worst case; its count has a cubic generating function, is the 3-Schröder sequence (OEIS A137842), and grows with base $\varphi^{5/2}\approx3.330$, below the Catalan base 4. We reduce maximality to an inequality on increments, verified to sixteen atoms, and explain why local exchange arguments cannot prove it. We also treat negation, exceptions, and background axioms, where normal-form uniqueness still decides equivalence but counting is open.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Almost Symmetric Linear Arc Monadic Datalog and Transitive Tournaments
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We introduce $n$-almost symmetric Datalog and study $n$-almost symmetric linear arc monadic Datalog. We characterize the finite relational structures whose constraint satisfaction problem is solved by this Datalog fragment as those that can be primitive positively constructed from the transitive tournament on $n+2$ vertices. We also give characterizations in terms of a certain homomorphism duality (which we call $n$-fixed unfolded caterpillar duality) and in universal-algebraic terms (the existence of $k$-absorptive operations and of operations forming an elevator chain of length $n+1$). This article generalizes the results from Bodirsky and Starke about symmetric linear arc monadic Datalog.

Signal Processing.title: Sensor Response-Time Reduction using Long-Short Term Memory Network Forecasting
Signal Processing.summary: The response time of a biosensor is a crucial metric in safety-critical applications such as medical diagnostics where an earlier diagnosis can markedly improve patient outcomes. However, the speed at which a biosensor reaches a final equilibrium state can be limited by poor mass transport and long molecular diffusion times that increase the time it takes target molecules to reach the active sensing region of a biosensor. While optimization of system and sensor design can promote molecules reaching the sensing element faster, a simpler and complementary approach for response time reduction that is widely applicable across all sensor platforms is to use time-series forecasting to predict the ultimate steady-state sensor response. In this work, we show that ensembles of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks can accurately predict equilibrium biosensor response from a small quantity of initial time-dependent biosensor measurements, allowing for significant reduction in response time by a mean and median factor of improvement of 18.6 and 5.1 respectively. The ensemble of models simultaneously estimates uncertainty, which is vital for ensuring confidence in the predictions and subsequent safety-related decisions that are made. This approach is demonstrated on real-time experimental data collected by exposing porous silicon biosensors to buffered protein solutions using a multi-channel fluidic cell that enables the automated measurement of 100 porous silicon biosensors in parallel. The dramatic improvement in sensor response time achieved using LSTM network ensembles and associated uncertainty quantification opens the door to trustworthy and faster responding biosensors, enabling more rapid medical diagnostics for faster clinical decision making that can lead to improved patient outcomes and healthcare access, as well as quicker identification of toxins in food and the environment.
Signal Processing.comment: 12 pages, 6 figures

Signal Processing.title: Adaptive Virtual PIN-Button Recognition on Passive NFC Cards via Domain Adaptation and Uncertainty Quantification
Signal Processing.summary: Passive Near Field Communication (NFC) cards are widely used for access control and authentication but provide no native interface for reliable user input. Radio-frequency (RF)-based interaction recognition offers a way to enable input on these cards, but hardware-dependent signal variations across cards and readers limit recognition reliability. This paper presents a practical virtual input framework that enables reliable PIN-button entry on passive NFC cards using a 12-button interface without modifying the commercial NFC card or the ISO/IEC 15693 communication protocol. We develop a multi-domain adaptation framework that jointly learns interaction representations invariant to both card and reader variations. To improve decision reliability, we introduce a model-agnostic uncertainty quantification framework based on conformal prediction that estimates recognition confidence. When confidence is insufficient, the system requests re-input; otherwise, accepted inputs are immediately confirmed through reader feedback, enabling reliable user interaction. A Software-Defined Radio (SDR)-based ISO/IEC 15693 testbed is developed using multiple commercial NFC cards and reader configurations. Experimental results show that domain adaptation improves recognition accuracy from 93.75% to 95.42% for the deep learning (DL) model and from 85.00% to 89.11% for the Random Forest model. Conformal prediction further enables adaptive high-confidence recognition, achieving average recognition accuracies of 96.85% and 90.55% for the DL and Random Forest models, respectively, across diverse hardware configurations.
Signal Processing.comment: Extended version of work presented at IEEE SECON 2026. Submitted to IEEE Internet of Things Journal

Signal Processing.title: Landscape Analysis of Simultaneous Blind Deconvolution and Phase Retrieval via Structured Low-Rank Tensor Recovery
Signal Processing.summary: This paper studies the landscape of the simultaneous blind deconvolution and phase retrieval (BDPR) problem via a structured low-rank tensor recovery framework. Since the complicated sensing structure makes direct landscape analysis technically challenging, we introduce a tractable tensor sensing surrogate that preserves the essential low-rank structure. We first analyze its population risk, characterize the global landscape on the unit sphere, and establish local linear convergence of Riemannian gradient descent (RGD) under mild conditions. We then extend the analysis to tensor sensing under a tensor restricted isometry property (TRIP), establishing local geometric and RGD convergence guarantees, and quantify robustness to measurement noise. Our theoretical results are further supported by extensive numerical experiments. These findings offer insights into the optimization landscape of the surrogate tensor sensing problem, thereby providing guidance for studying and solving the original BDPR problem.
Signal Processing.comment: Revised version; 30 pages, 6 figures, plus 31 pages of supplementary material

Signal Processing.title: Neuromorphic Decoding and Dynamical Image Reconstruction from Populations of Spiking Retinal Ganglion Cells
Signal Processing.summary: Decoding visual stimuli from the spiking activity of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) informs both our understanding of the retinal code and the design of visual prostheses. Natural vision is dynamic, yet state-of-the-art decoders mostly reconstruct single frames with artificial neural networks that process dense, continuous-valued signals rather than the retina's sparse, asynchronous spikes. We asked whether dynamic scenes can be reconstructed and tracked entirely within the spike domain, and at what computational cost. We built an end-to-end spiking neural network (SNN) whose neurons integrate the recorded RGC spikes over time. Populations of up to 1836 RGCs were recorded ex vivo from mouse retina on high-density microelectrode arrays while flashed images, moving bars, drifting gratings and randomly moving handwritten digits were presented. For moving digits, one shared spiking encoder fed two readouts, one reconstructing the image and one decoding the digit's position. Compute energy was estimated from counted synaptic operations. The SNN decoded what and where at once. It reconstructed the stimuli with a structural similarity (SSIM) of up to 0.93, refining the reconstruction as spikes accumulated, and tracked a randomly moving target with a mean error of 1.33 pixels on a $32\times32$ grid. Its fidelity nearly matched that of the best of 17 larger spiking and artificial decoders (5.9 million to 1.7 billion parameters, versus 5.4 million), and at a mean firing rate of 14.2% it needed an estimated $\sim$70-fold less compute energy than a dense artificial network of the same architecture. Dynamic visual scenes can thus be decoded from retinal population activity in the spike domain, with a compact network and at a compute cost compatible with implantable and wearable neural interfaces, supporting spike-native decoders for visual prostheses.

Signal Processing.title: Exact signal recovery from generative priors with sigmoid output activation
Signal Processing.summary: We show exact signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for feedforward neural networks with piecewise-linear activations and a final sigmoid activation, with no assumption of expansivity. Consider a ReLU network of depth $d$ with a sigmoid final activation, whose input layer, of dimension $k$, is the narrowest, and let $K$ be the geometric mean of the widths of its layers. We show that, with high probability, all signals of the range whose entries lie in $[δ, 1 - δ]$ are uniformly recovered from $m \gtrsim k(d \log(K/k) + \log(1+\log(1/δ)))$ measurements.
Signal Processing.comment: 9 pages

Signal Processing.title: Untangling Dense Crowds with mmWave Radar: From Crowd Semantics to Individual Spatial Behaviors
Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we present a novel framework for recovering individual footprints and pedestrian spatial behaviors in dense crowds. This is a highly challenging problem, as pedestrians can merge or block one another often and for prolonged periods in crowded areas, leading to strongly entangled observations. Our approach jointly leverages learned crowd semantics and principled reasoning over persistent radar observability loss to systematically infer individual spatial footprints. At the macroscopic level, we learn spatial usage patterns of the crowd from radar point clouds, while at the microscopic level we develop a physics-informed model of radar observability loss caused by sustained merging and occlusion. Building on this macro-micro structure, we introduce a semantic-guided multi-hypothesis reasoning foundation that evaluates competing hypotheses via principled reasoning over many-to-one and one-to-none observation mappings, enabling untangling of individual spatial footprints. We evaluate the framework through 18 real-world experiments using an off-the-shelf mmWave radar, involving crowds of up to (and including) 10 individuals across six categories of diverse pedestrian behaviors, and four environments. Our methodology robustly recovers individual spatial footprints, even during prolonged and persistent observability loss, demonstrating strong structural consistency with the ground-truth. The recovered footprints further enable accurate zonal analysis of pedestrian space usage. Finally, we present an ablation study and further compare against state-of-the-art. The proposed foundation substantially outperforms the state-of-the-art across all experiments, achieving an average median DTW of 0.31 m compared to 0.96 m, highlighting the framework's robustness to frequent and prolonged merging and occlusion.

Signal Processing.title: Markov State-Space Modeling and Channel Characterization for DNA-Based Molecular Communication
Signal Processing.summary: DNA-based molecular communication with microarray-style reception under reversible hybridization is of interest for emerging DNA-enabled sensing and Internet of Bio-Nano Things (IoBNT) systems. In such channels, the bound-state observation exhibits both inter-symbol interference (ISI) and colored counting noise. To capture these effects in a communication-oriented form, we develop a Markov state-space framework based on a voxelized reaction-diffusion model, in which a block-structured transition matrix describes molecular transport and binding/unbinding dynamics. For the microarray specialization, this representation yields the channel impulse response (CIR), the equilibrium gain, and a settling-time-based characterization of the effective channel memory. Building on the resulting symbol-rate observation model for on-off keying, we derive a grouped-binomial counting model and obtain a closed-form expression for the covariance of the counting noise. Based on these statistics, we further develop a differential-threshold detector and a finite-memory decision-feedback equalizer and benchmark them against a symbol-by-symbol maximum a posteriori detector with decision feedback (MAP-DF). Numerical results validate the theoretical correlation behavior and show that the relative performance of the proposed receivers depends strongly on the channel-memory regime.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Internet of Things Journal. 25 pages, includes supplementary material

Signal Processing.title: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment
Signal Processing.summary: Non-invasive brain-to-text interfaces offer alternative communication pathways for people with communication disabilities. However, sentence-level decoding from electroencephalography (EEG) remains challenging. We propose a hierarchical EEG-text alignment framework that retrieves sentences by progressively decoding coarse-grained semantic information and fine-grained sentence representations. We hypothesize that broader semantic context can be more reliably captured from EEG than individual sentences. Accordingly, EEG representations are first aligned with semantic classes, followed by sentence retrieval within the predicted class. Among over 2,000 unique text samples, our approach achieves average top-5 and top-10 retrieval accuracies of 62.6\% $\pm$ 1.0\% and 83.5\% $\pm$ 1.0\%, respectively, compared with 50.3\% $\pm$ 2.3\% and 68.3\% $\pm$ 2.0\% for direct EEG-sentence alignment. Qualitative analysis further reveals that decoding performance depends strongly on textual context. These findings demonstrate the potential of hierarchical semantic alignment for improving sentence-level EEG-to-text decoding.

Signal Processing.title: Benchmarking Sensor-Fault Robustness in Forecasting
Signal Processing.summary: Cyber-physical system (CPS) forecasting models depend on sensor streams with noisy, biased, missing, or temporally misaligned readings, yet standard forecasting evaluation often selects models by nominal error without showing whether they remain robust under such faults. We introduce SensorFault-Bench, a CPS-grounded protocol that evaluates forecasting architectures and robustness-improvement methods through controlled synthetic stress tests of isolated input faults, together with an operational taxonomy of the methods. Across four real-world datasets and eight scored scenarios governed by a standardized severity model, it reports worst-scenario degradation, clean mean squared error (MSE), and worst-scenario fault-time MSE, separating relative robustness from absolute error. Explicit fault-training methods train on adjacent fault families disjoint from the scored scenarios. Empirically, forecasting architectures favored by clean MSE can degrade sharply under faults, and clean-MSE rankings can disagree with worst-scenario fault-time error rankings. Chronos-2, the evaluated zero-shot foundation model, matches or trails the last-value naive forecaster in clean MSE on the two single-target datasets and has the largest worst-scenario degradation on ETTh1 and Traffic, where all channels are forecast targets. For the evaluated robustness-improvement method set, paired deltas show selective degradation reductions: projected gradient descent adversarial training and randomized training lead where value faults dominate observed degradation, and fault augmentation leads on Traffic, where availability faults dominate. High degradation reveals fault sensitivity that clean MSE misses, while low degradation supports robustness only within the evaluated scenarios. The benchmark therefore screens forecasters before use in a specific deployment, which requires validation against its recorded faults.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track. 67 pages, 6 figures, 38 tables. Code: https://github.com/awindmann/SensorFault-Bench

Signal Processing.title: The Confidence Score: a New Measure on Kernels
Signal Processing.summary: Across a wide range of applications, kernel measures are used to tune hyperparameters, select among candidate kernels, and assess the suitability of kernels for specific learning tasks. For classification, kernel measures are used to predict which kernels may produce accurate kernel classifiers. Many existing kernel measures, such as alignment to the ideal kernel, are designed to reward kernels which captures all samples from the same class as similar. While effective in many settings, this requirement is unnecessarily restrictive for classification, where classes may exhibit substantial internal structure. In this work, the "Confidence Score", a new kernel measure, is proposed. Unlike alignment-to-the-ideal kernel measures, the Confidence Score measures the alignment between an encoding of the ground truth and that ground truth projected by the kernel, allowing kernels that preserve intra-class structure to achieve high scores. Through experiments, it is demonstrated that the Confidence Score exhibits a higher correlation with classification accuracy across a variety of kernels on both real-world and synthetic datasets, compared to select other kernel measures.
Signal Processing.comment: 27 pages

Signal Processing.title: Spectrum Sharing Among Broadband LEO Mega-Constellations: Interference Regulations and Coexistence Mechanisms
Signal Processing.summary: Thousands of broadband LEO satellites are now in orbit with thousands more on the way, all operating under non-exclusive spectrum allocations across the Ku-, Ka-, and Q/V-bands. To govern this shared spectrum, regulators recently enacted protection constraints that cap instantaneous interference levels and time-averaged throughput degradation. In this article, we review the governing FCC and ITU regulatory frameworks and dissect this interference environment. We examine practical non-cooperative coexistence mechanisms, highlighting how dynamic satellite selection and passive ground sensing circumvent the physical limits of beamforming alone. We then evaluate potential cooperative coordination architectures spanning centralized registries and bilateral interfaces. Finally, we analyze key open challenges: scaling beyond two networks, mitigating feeder link contention from direct-to-cell systems, rerouting traffic over optical inter-satellite links, and modernizing international sharing policies.

Signal Processing.title: Outage Probability Analysis of MRC-Based Fluid Antenna Systems under Rician Fading
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates a fluid antenna system (FAS) where a single-antenna transmitter communicates with a receiver equipped with a fluid antenna (FA) over Rician fading channels. Two channel models are considered to incorporate the correlation among the ports into the fading gains, namely: i) the widely used physical reference port model, implemented by considering the first physical port as the reference port; and ii) the virtual reference port model, considering a common port correlation coefficient and implemented by assuming the presence of a virtual reference port. Assuming that multiple ports among the M available FA ports can be activated, the receiver selects the best K with the highest instantaneous signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and combines the received signals at the selected ports using maximum ratio combining. For both port models, the statistics of the post-combining SNR are derived using a characteristic function approach, which allows to analyze the outage probabilities (OPs) of the FAS. Additional closed-form lower bounds on the OPs and the asymptotic OPs at high SNR are derived, revealing the diversity order of the FAS to be M. Numerical results validate the analytical framework and demonstrate the interplay of key system parameters on the performance of the considered MRC-based FAS. Specifically, the performance difference between the two reference port models becomes increasingly evident as M, K, and the average SNR of the FAS increase.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures

Signal Processing.title: Do Ray-Traced Cities Make a Better Channel Prior for an Unseen Site? A Pre-Registered Study in Simulation, and a Test on Measured Channels that Reverses It
Signal Processing.summary: Channel estimators at a newly deployed base station usually start from 3GPP stochastic channel models, which describe no particular street. We ask whether a channel prior pooled from many ray-traced cities serves an unseen site better than the 3GPP CDL models, and whether learned estimators make the difference. With Sionna RT on 14 city scenes, LMMSE estimation from covariance priors, leave-one-city-out evaluation, and pass/fail bars written down before each main experiment, we find in simulation that the pooled prior sits about 0.6 dB from a site-trained estimator with no site measurements, about what CDL reaches after 50 measurements. Learned models added little: at most 0.65 dB in estimation, and in channel prediction a simple classical method beat CNN predictors by 1.8-12 dB from 2 ms ahead. On measured channels from the DICHASUS outdoor dataset (1.272 GHz, three 2x8 arrays on one building) the result reversed: the pooled ray-traced prior was 3.2-4.1 dB worse than CDL. The simulated channels were too clean; with users at the real distances, even a scattering level tuned from 50 site measurements left the prior about 2 dB behind CDL. A pre-registered follow-on on two more measured environments found the generic CDL prior 2.1-4.7 dB from a site-trained one: no further in a factory hall than on the street, furthest in a small lab room. Finally, a hallway model calibrated to measurements by differentiable ray tracing reproduced delay spread, but as a prior in an unmeasured part of the hallway it was 4.5 dB worse than CDL on the full array. All measured results come from one sounder.
Signal Processing.comment: 11 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables

Signal Processing.title: Characterizing the vertical continuity of fuel strata based on TLS point clouds Gaussian decomposition and overlap metrics
Signal Processing.summary: Vertical forest structure influences fire behavior by regulating understory-to-canopy fuel connectivity, yet operational fuel-type models represent this complexity through discrete classes that only indirectly capture vertical continuity. High-density point clouds offer an opportunity to characterize vertical fuel connectivity in a more explicit and continuous manner, but specific methodological approaches are still required. We applied Gaussian decomposition to vertical height profiles derived from terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) point clouds across 25 permanent forest plots to characterize geometric vertical fuel continuity. A multiscale analysis spanning from the plot scale to ~0.5 $m^2$ units was used to evaluate geometric, probabilistic, and overlap metrics for characterizing fuel strata. The method reproduced the vertical transition between shrub and tree strata, with median Pearson correlations ranging from 0.83 to 0.96 across analysis levels. Probability density overlap metrics and separability indicators, such as the Jeffries-Matusita distance, provided complementary descriptors of vertical continuity. Intermediate spatial scales (3-6 m cells) provided a useful compromise between spatial detail and the consistent representation of shrub-canopy interaction patterns. Finer scales increased variability due to point density reduction and profile irregularity, and low mean squared error values were found insufficient as sole performance indicators. Gaussian decomposition applied to TLS point clouds enables explicit quantification of vertical fuel continuity, a limitation of current discrete classification systems. Continuous vertical connectivity metrics derived from this approach offer a pathway for improving ladder fuel characterization and strengthening decision-making support in wildfire risk assessment.
Signal Processing.comment: 45 pages, 15 figures Author affiliations and ORCID: Jesús Torralba https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8644-8604 , Luis Á. Ruiz https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0073-7259 , Pablo Crespo-Peremarch https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2241-4493 , Marina Simó-Martí https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9605-9645 , Juan Pedro Carbonell-Rivera https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6724-6780

Signal Processing.title: 6G ISAC Drone Detection: Signal Processing and Experimental Validation at FR1
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) enables mobile networks to detect passive targets such as drones at minimal additional cost. However, in ISAC, a small drone must be detected against strong ground clutter with the limited radio resources left by communications. In this paper, we propose two ISAC target detectors: a coherent detector, which combines all frames and beam dwells of a revisit, and a non-coherent detector, robust to inter-frame clock phase drift. The algorithms leverage per-dwell clutter whitening and the adaptive coherence estimator (ACE) detection statistic to improve performance. Both detectors estimate the range, radial velocity, and azimuth of targets in real time on a laptop graphics processing unit (GPU). Measurements with an FR1 ISAC proof-of-concept system based on a commercial base station show that the coherent detector outperforms the non-coherent one and recovers the full track.

Signal Processing.title: On the Learnability of Footwear Robustness: Footstep Recognition Under Unseen Conditions
Signal Processing.summary: Footstep patterns, captured using pressure or force-sensitive walkways during natural walking, offer a convenient and passive approach to biometric recognition. However, footwear variability poses a major challenge to practical deployment, as it impacts both the foot-sensor interface and the user's underlying gait mechanics. This study considers the particularly difficult scenario where users enroll under one fixed footwear condition but must later be recognized in arbitrary, unseen footwear. Using the StepUP-P150 dataset, we show that footwear-induced shift, while substantial and heterogeneous across individuals, contains shared structure that can be learned from a training population and transferred, zero-shot, to previously unseen users and footwear styles. We do this using BiStepNet, a novel architecture that decomposes spatial and temporal identity cues into independently trainable streams and outperforms compact 3D spatiotemporal baselines for cross-footwear recognition. We demonstrate that cross-footwear recognition performance scales systematically with the volume and diversity of footwear representation in the training set, with gains transferring to footwear styles not directly observed during training. Moreover, we show that auxiliary gait datasets with only partial modality overlap (incorporated through the architecture's decomposed design) can be leveraged to further improve robustness to unseen footwear conditions.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages (+2 pages supplementary), 7 figures

Signal Processing.title: Noise Parameter Identification in Ensemble of Atomic Clocks
Signal Processing.summary: The paper introduces a parameter identification framework for atomic clock ensembles, where individual clocks are represented by second-order linear stochastic state-space model. The proposed procedure relies exclusively on differential measurements, namely the pairwise phase differences between a designated pivot clock and the remaining ensemble members. The identification targets key parameters for each clock: white and random-walk frequency noise variances, constant frequency drift, and (co)variance of the measurement noise. To identify these parameters, two distinct identification methods are proposed. Their estimation accuracy is rigorously demonstrated via numerical simulations and validated using empirical data from atomic hydrogen maser (AHM) clocks at ESTEC Timing Laboratory.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON ULTRASONICS, FERROELECTRICS, AND FREQUENCY CONTROL

Signal Processing.title: Interpretability Analysis of End-to-End Learned CSI Feedback for Precoding-Oriented Massive MIMO
Signal Processing.summary: Recent end-to-end learning frameworks jointly optimize pilot design, channel state information (CSI) feedback, and downlink precoding, achieving strong performance under limited feedback overhead in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks. However, the internal representations and decision-making strategies learned by these architectures remain largely unexplored. This paper presents an interpretability analysis of a precoding-oriented end-to-end CSI feedback framework using explainable artificial intelligence (xAI) techniques. Building on a validated learned architecture, we investigate the structure of the learned pilots, latent feedback representations, and precoding vectors through low-dimensional visualization, density-based clustering, and cross-block representation analysis. The results reveal that the learned system undergoes a transition as the feedback constraint is relaxed. Under stringent feedback budgets, the encoder develops clustered latent representations and quantized precoding behavior. As additional feedback resources become available, the learned representations evolve into smooth geometry-preserving manifolds that retain physically meaningful channel characteristics such as dominant angular information, while enabling more adaptive precoding decisions. Furthermore, the learned pilot signals naturally form complementary sensing patterns aligned with the underlying channel statistics. The analysis also reveals a shift from gain-driven beamforming strategies under severe compression to increasingly interference-aware precoding as the feedback budget increases. These findings provide new insight into how end-to-end learned CSI feedback systems balance compression efficiency and communication performance and establish a general framework for interpreting learned communication architectures.

Signal Processing.title: Joint Channel Scanning and Geometry-Aware Codebook Design for Movable Antenna Arrays
Signal Processing.summary: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems rely on spatial degrees of freedom, but fixed antenna geometries cannot adapt to propagation environments. Movable antenna (MA) systems address this by adapting antenna positions to the channel. In discrete MA architectures, active antennas are selected from candidate positions, requiring channel state information (CSI) at those positions. With limited radio-frequency (RF) chains, CSI is acquired through successive pilot rounds, or antenna scanning, whose overhead can offset reconfiguration gains. This paper studies discrete MA geometry optimization when only a fraction of candidate positions is scanned. We show that a geometry-aware (GA) steering-vector codebook, constructed from the actual antenna coordinates, reconstructs channels more accurately than a conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT) codebook when the optimized array departs from a uniform grid. We then show that the scanning fraction required to approach full-scan sum-rate performance depends on the CSI acquisition method: least-squares (LS) estimation degrades sharply under sparse scanning, while codebook-based acquisition remains robust. We also propose an adaptive scanning procedure that probes candidates in batches and stops automatically using the acquired pilots, avoiding a preset scanning budget. Finally, we quantify sum-rate losses as users move from their initial positions and evaluate recovery through re-scanning and geometry re-selection, relative to fixed-aperture operation with outdated or fresh CSI. Numerical results show that adaptive scanning achieves about 99.5% of the full-scan sum rate while scanning only 11% of candidate positions.

Signal Processing.title: Sparse Channel Estimation and Signal Recovery for Reduced-PAPR Visible Light Optical OFDM Systems Relying on Bayesian Learning
Signal Processing.summary: A multipath CIR estimator is proposed, followed by sparse frequency-domain (FD) signal detection, which harnesses the simultaneous-sparsity innate in the multipath CIR and FD signals across measurement vectors, conceived for optical OFDM (O-OFDM) utilized for visible light communication (VLC) systems having reduced peak-to-average power ratio. At the outset, we derive the input-output relationships for the asymmetrically clipped O-OFDM (ACO-OFDM) as well as for the direct current-biased O-OFDM (DCO-OFDM) systems. Next, traditional benchmarking methods are introduced for channel estimation (CE), including both the LMMSE and LS methods, followed by an orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP)-based technique capable of exploiting sparsity in the multipath CIR of the VLC system. Subsequently, an CE technique based on a novel group sparse OMP (GOMP) concept is proposed, which capitalizes on the group-sparsity in the delay domain of the CIR across measurement vectors, attributed to the multipath characteristics inherent in the NLoS components of the VLC channel model. Additionally, an advanced group-sparse CE technique is put forth based on the group-sparse Bayesian learning (GBL) approach, which considerably reduces the pilot overhead. A low complexity version of GBL, termed LCGBL, is also developed that reduces the computational cost of GBL significantly. Consequently, the GOMP and GBL frameworks are also extended to the data detection of the sparse FD O-OFDM symbols, which utilizes the group-sparsity of the FD O-OFDM symbols across measurement vectors. The Bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound (BCRLB) is computed to assess the estimation performance of the proposed CE techniques. Our simulations demonstrate that, despite its reduced pilot overhead, the proposed GBL technique outperforms the other CE schemes in terms of its BER, outage probability, and NMSE, quantitatively reinforcing its superiority.

Signal Processing.title: Current-Future Rate Tradeoffs in ISAC Under Random Path Changes
Signal Processing.summary: In mobile wireless links, motion changes path directions and visibility, and blockage can shift communication to a different propagation path. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) allows a base station (BS) to use echoes of data transmissions to monitor these changes and guide subsequent beam selection. Illuminating objects that govern future path availability may reduce the beamforming gain on the current communication route. Existing sensing-communication tradeoffs and dynamic beam-control frameworks do not directly quantify the future communication gain from this current-rate sacrifice. We quantify sensing value by the future-rate gain enabled by echo-adaptive beam selection. We derive explicit expressions for the future communication gain and the net gain after accounting for the current-rate loss. The analysis uses a coupled communication-echo channel with binary-state Markov motion over a finite burst informed by one processed echo. We show that monitoring is worthwhile when its future-rate gain exceeds the current loss, while more informative observations yield zero additional future rate if they cannot change any future optimal beam. We derive interpretable gain bounds exposing the roles of improved scene discrimination, motion memory and future beam-rate differences. Reciprocal-channel tests demonstrate positive net accumulated-rate gains from monitoring a moving blocker during reflected-path service, including continuous position uncertainty.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures

Signal Processing.title: A Unified Pulse-Shaped OFDM Framework for Chirp-Domain Waveforms: Continuous-Time Modeling and Practical I/O Analysis
Signal Processing.summary: A unified framework for chirp-domain waveforms, including orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) and affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM), is developed. Their continuous-time representations are shown to fall within the conventional Weyl-Heisenberg (WH) framework for multicarrier waveforms, with the root chirp as the prototype pulse. Since the root chirp has constant envelope and is transparent to subcarrier orthogonality, these waveforms can be further interpreted as pulse-shaped (PS) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, whose power spectral density is derived analytically. The derived spectrum reveals that implementations based on the discrete affine Fourier transform rely on sub-Nyquist samples and exhibit frequency aliasing. We prove that the corresponding aliased chirps are only conditionally orthogonal, whereas sample-wise root-Nyquist pulse shaping of the discrete-time AFDM (DT-AFDM) sequence produces mutually orthogonal pulse-shaped chirps, resulting in the pulse-shaped AFDM (PS-AFDM) waveform. We then derive an exact waveform-level input-output (I/O) relation for PS-AFDM over delay-Doppler (DD) channels, showing that the effective channel at a practical receiver is generally not a superposition of pure path-wise DD components. Waveform simulations verify the derived relation to machine precision, while the conventional sequence-level I/O relation for DT-AFDM exhibits a substantial mismatch with waveform behavior for practical channels with continuous-valued delays.
Signal Processing.comment: 14 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications. The supplementary materials for this paper are available at: https://oddm.io

Signal Processing.title: Deep Plug-and-Play Proximal Distance Algorithm for Robust Principal Component Analysis
Signal Processing.summary: Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA) is essential in signal processing, with applications in hyperspectral imaging, face recognition, and video background modeling. Traditional RPCA methods often suffer from insufficient utilization of data priors and struggle to capture complex image structures. Conversely, advanced deep denoisers like DnCNN, FFDNet, and DRUNet excel at leveraging image data priors but lack physical model constraints and demonstrate poor robustness against structured noise in RPCA tasks. This paper proposes a novel Plug-and-Play (PnP) method for multi-channel RPCA, integrating both the physical generative model and cutting-edge deep priors. Extensive experiments on RGB and hyperspectral datasets show that PnP-PDA achieves better quantitative performance than conventional RPCA methods and state-of-the-art methods, including deep denoisers and tensor RPCA approaches, while preserving visual details.

Signal Processing.title: The Symmetric Location Problem: a Song of Efficiency and Robustness
Signal Processing.summary: The aim of this Lecture Note is to introduce the Signal Processing (SP) community to a powerful yet still under-utilised tool: the semiparametric statistics. In short, the semiparametric framework allows us to estimate or perform hypothesis testing on a finite-dimensional parameter $\boldsymbolθ \in Θ\subseteq \mathbb{R}^p$ in the presence of an \textit{infinite-dimensional nuisance parameter} $g \in \mathcal{S}$ (i.e. a function), such as the density of the noise. Clearly, this framework is general enough to include almost every SP application. Remarkably, as the title suggests drawing on George R. R. Martin's famous book series, the greatest advantage of semiparametric statistics over parametric and non-parametric ones lies in the fact that it is able to reconcile two seemingly dichotomous concepts: statistical efficiency and distributional robustness. To explain exactly what this means, in this Lecture Note we will focus our attention on the famous and fundamental symmetric location problem.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE Magazine "Lecture Notes"

Signal Processing.title: Directional Statistics in Signal Processing: A Geometry Driven Overview of Models, Learning, and Applications
Signal Processing.summary: Many signal-processing objects are defined by periodicity, normalization, sign or global-phase ambiguity, basis invariance, or positive-semidefinite constraints and therefore cannot be modeled faithfully in ordinary Euclidean space. This paper develops a geometry driven framework for directional statistics in signal processing, connecting signal representations to their natural manifolds or quotient spaces and to probability models compatible with their invariances. After reviewing instances of directional statistics in the signal processing literature, we review circular, toroidal, spherical, projective, Stiefel, Grassmann, and covariance-valued distributions, emphasizing their statistical assumptions, computational requirements, and dimensional limitations relevant to signal processing. We describe various modeling and estimation strategies, including analytical and gradient-based maximum likelihood, structured low-rank parameterizations, mixtures and hidden Markov models (HMMs), score-based and contrastive estimation, and geometry-aware K-means. To exemplify the consequences of geometry-aware modeling, we study multivariate phase coherence in synthetic data and functional neuroimaging, comparing toroidal phase vectors to projective, Grassmann, and positive-semidefinite representations. We also study speaker separation in a car environment, showing that directional representations outperform a standard Euclidean model. These examples demonstrate that when the geometric representation, statistical distribution, inference method, and computational regime are considered together, they have the potential to lead to improved models across a broad range of signal processing applications.

Signal Processing.title: Mutual-Coupling-Aware Joint Precoding and Antenna Positioning for Movable-Antenna MU-MIMO Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Movable antennas (MAs) improve wireless communications by adapting antenna positions to the propagation environment. However, antenna movement also changes the mutual coupling (MC) among elements of the transmit and receive arrays, which affects the performance of MA-enabled systems. In this paper, we investigate MC-aware joint precoding and antenna positioning for a downlink multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system with MAs at both the base station and users. We establish an MC-aware system model by combining field-response propagation with a circuit-based representation of the transmit and receive arrays. Based on this model, we formulate a weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization problem that jointly optimizes multi-stream precoders and antenna positions. The problem is challenging because the precoders and positions are coupled through the propagation channels and position-dependent MC matrices. To address this challenge, we reformulate the problem in the antenna-current domain to to efficiently handle the MC matrices and develop a current-domain weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) framework for alternating optimization. Furthermore, we handle the nonconvex position updates within the framework by using majorization--minimization (MM) and solve the resulting convex subproblems with a dedicated conic alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design improves the WSR over both an MC-aware fixed array and a movable-array design that ignores MC during optimization.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, submitted to an IEEE Journal for possible publication

Signal Processing.title: Movable Antenna Aided Robust Wireless Transmission: From Model-Based Optimization to Scalable Reinforcement Learning
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates robust joint antenna positioning and precoding for multiuser movable antenna (MA) systems under imperfect channel state information (CSI). First, we identify the mismatch between the spatial statistics of densely sampled MA channels and the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) basis used for conventional robust precoding. To address this, we develop a novel discrete prolate spheroidal sequence (DPSS)-based a posteriori channel model. By exploiting the spatial covariance structure of MA channels, this model is better suited to modeling MA channel uncertainty. Building on this model, we develop an efficient iterative algorithm for robust joint antenna positioning and precoding to maximize the expected sum rate. By transforming the coupled optimization of antenna positioning and precoding at each iteration into direct comparisons of closed-form scores, we design a low-complexity position replacement scheme that effectively reuses matrix computations across candidate sets. To further improve efficiency and scalability, we exploit the inherent tensor equivariance (TE) of the problem to develop a reinforcement learning framework. To explicitly account for channel uncertainty, we develop novel pairwise user-interaction and CSI-conditioned equivariant attention mechanisms to encode channel statistics and adaptively fuse them with the available CSI. We further introduce distance-biased spatial attention to incorporate the geometry of candidate positions into attention weighting, thereby enhancing spatial feature learning. Simulation results show that the proposed methods improve sum-rate performance while reducing online runtime under imperfect CSI. These methods also achieve near-optimal performance under perfect CSI, closely matching the exhaustive-search method. Moreover, the learning framework generalizes across different numbers of users and MAs without retraining.
Signal Processing.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Signal Processing.title: Domain-Adaptive Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding for Image Classification
Signal Processing.summary: Deep joint source--channel coding (Deep JSCC) can suffer from domain shift between training and deployment data. We study single-source domain adaptation for image classification over wireless channels. A Gaussian example shows that improving channel quality does not necessarily improve target-domain accuracy under a fixed source-trained classifier. We further proposed an information objective to reduce domain information while preserving class information. Motivated by the analysis, we develop a domain-adaptive Deep JSCC method that combines class-wise adversarial alignment with pseudo-label supervised contrastive learning. The former uses all target samples to reduce class-conditional domain differences, while the latter selects high-confidence target samples to obtain class-discriminative received representations. We relate these losses to the information objective, and analyze the effects of pseudo-label errors and confidence-based selection. Experiments on SVHN--MNIST and PACS over AWGN and Rayleigh channels demonstrate improved target-domain classification without additional inference-time networks. The proposed method achieves 98.15\% accuracy on SVHN $\rightarrow$ MNIST at 10~dB CSNR.

Signal Processing.title: SpellerSSL: Self-Supervised Learning with P300 Aggregation for Speller BCIs
Signal Processing.summary: Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based P300 speller brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) face three main challenges: low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), poor generalization, and time-consuming calibration. We propose SpellerSSL, a framework that combines self-supervised learning (SSL) with P300 aggregation to address these issues. First, we introduce an aggregation strategy to enhance SNR. Second, to achieve generalization in training, we employ a customized 1D U-Net backbone and pre-train the model on both cross-domain and in-domain EEG data. The pretrained model is subsequently fine-tuned with a lightweight ERP-Head classifier for P300 detection, which adapts the learned representations to subject-specific data. Our evaluations on calibration time demonstrate that combining the aggregation strategy with SSL significantly reduces the calibration burden per subject and improves robustness across subjects. Experimental results show that SSL learns effective EEG representations in both in-domain and cross-domain, with in-domain achieving a state-of-the-art character recognition rate of 94% with only 7 repetitions and the highest information transfer rate (ITR) of 21.86 bits/min on the public II-B dataset. Moreover, in-domain SSL with P300 aggregation reduces the required calibration size by 60% while maintaining a comparable character recognition rate. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to apply SSL to P300 spellers, highlighting its potential to improve both efficiency and generalization in speller BCIs and paving the way toward an EEG foundation model for P300 speller BCIs. The code is available at: https://github.com/Emotiv/SpellerSSL-NeurIPS2025
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Data on the Brain & Mind (DBM)

Signal Processing.title: Toward Generalized LEO Channel Prediction: A Rapid Adaptation Time-Frequency Mamba Framework
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate channel state information (CSI) prediction is pivotal for enhancing system capacity in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite-terrestrial communications within the sixth-generation vision of global ubiquitous connectivity. However, the extreme mobility of LEO satellites, coupled with significant propagation delays, induces severe channel aging. Existing deep learning (DL) methods often struggle with non-stationary dynamics or generalize poorly across diverse global geographies. To address these challenges, we design the Evo-TFMamba, which is an evolutionary framework integrating time-frequency selective Mamba blocks with meta-learning for generalized CSI prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Evo-TFMamba performs adaptive prediction according to the geographic coverage of LEO satellites. Meanwhile, it significantly enhances the model's generalization ability, particularly when faced with unseen channel environments in LEO satellite communication.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, IEEE Global Communications Conference (GLOBECOM) 2026

Signal Processing.title: A Survey on Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces Towards Practical Deployments: Security and Privacy Perspectives
Signal Processing.summary: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a transformative technology capable of reshaping wireless environments through dynamic manipulation of electromagnetic waves. Although RISs have been widely studied for communication, sensing, and localization, their security and privacy implications are still fragmented across application-specific studies, prototypes, and testbeds. This survey provides a deployment-oriented review of RIS applications, with a focus on the security and privacy threats, vulnerabilities, and defensive strategies relevant to practical use. We analyze scenarios with two types of systems (with and without legitimate RIS) and two types of attackers (with and without malicious RIS), and clarify how RIS introduces new attack surfaces to practical systems, including eavesdropping, jamming, and spoofing attacks. In response, we review defenses against RIS-related attacks in these systems, such as protocol- and algorithm-level protections, unauthorized RIS detection, and interference/disruption-based mitigation. We also discuss scenarios in which the legitimate user applies an additional RIS to defend against attacks. To support future research, we also curate papers and available open resources at https://awesome-ris-security.github.io/. By highlighting RIS's functionality and its security/privacy challenges and opportunities, this survey aims to guide researchers and engineers toward the development of secure, resilient, and privacy-preserving RIS-enabled practical wireless systems and environments.
Signal Processing.comment: 35 pages, 17 figures, 13 tables. Survey article on security and privacy in RIS-enabled systems

Signal Processing.title: Dielectric Models of Normal and Diseased Human Trabecular Bones at Microwave Frequencies
Signal Processing.summary: The dielectric properties of biological tissues are used to investigate the interaction of electromagnetic (EM) fields with the human body. These properties are integrated into EM numerical simulations, such as the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, using dielectric models such as Cole-Cole and Debye models. These computational tools are employed to study the propagation of EM waves within the human body. This paper has developed the one-pole and two-pole Cole-Cole and Debye models for the dielectric properties of normal and diseased human trabecular bone tissue at microwave frequencies (0.5-8.5 GHz). The dielectric properties of normal trabecular and cortical bone were derived based on the literature, while those of diseased human trabecular bones (osteoporotic and osteoarthritis) were acquired from a previous study conducted by the authors, which characterised the properties within the 0.5-8.5 GHz frequency range. This study has employed a weighted least squares method to optimise the one-pole and two-pole dielectric models' parameters. The accuracy of the developed dielectric models is validated by comparing the simulated results with the experimental data already published by the authors. The comparative analysis of the models demonstrated that the one-pole Cole-Cole model achieved a better fit compared to the one-pole Debye model across all bone types. Additionally, the two-pole Cole-Cole model exhibited a better fit than the two-pole Debye model. The proposed models can be used in numerical simulations to investigate the interaction of EM fields with bone tissue and develop and optimise microwave bone health monitoring and treatment techniques.
Signal Processing.comment: 12 pages, 9 figures, 8 tables. Published in IEEE Open Journal of Antennas and Propagation (open access, CC BY 4.0)

Signal Processing.title: SPIRE: Shared-Private Representation Learning for Continuous Multi-Region LFP under Perturbation
Signal Processing.summary: Learning shared and region-specific representations from continuous multi-region local field potentials (LFPs) is challenging because neural signals are nonlinear, autocorrelated, spectrally structured, and temporally misaligned. We introduce SPIRE (Shared-Private Inter-Regional Encoder), a nonlinear, time-resolved framework that separates multi-region LFP into shared and region-specific latent trajectories using region-specific sequence encoders, constrained temporal alignment, shared-only reconstruction, and variance regularization. On synthetic benchmarks with known ground-truth factors, SPIRE preferentially recovers shared and private information despite nonlinear mixing, time-varying delays, and spectral confounding. On held-out human GPi-STN LFP, shared representations strongly predict activity across regions, while cross-region prediction from private representations remains near a structured temporal null, supporting functional rather than strict statistical separation. We then apply representations trained on off-stimulation recordings to deep brain stimulation (DBS) data. Stimulation induces larger changes and more strongly encodes stimulation condition in shared than private representations. A matched CTAE analysis reproduces the shared-over-private effect, while retaining substantially less stimulation information. These findings suggest that DBS-related changes are preferentially expressed in neural representations shared across recorded regions.
Signal Processing.comment: 37 pages total. Main paper (including references): 13 pages with 3 figures and 4 tables. Appendix: 24 pages with 14 figures and 14 tables. Submitted to ICLR 2027

Signal Processing.title: Reconfigurable Antenna-Enhanced ISAC: A Unified Perspective on Electromagnetic Adaptation
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables sensing and communication (S&C) functions to share time, frequency, and hardware resources, offering an efficient paradigm for next-generation wireless systems. However, conventional fixed-configuration antenna (FCA) architectures provide limited flexibility in adapting the physical electromagnetic (EM) response of the end-to-end wireless link. This article develops a unified EM-adaptation perspective on reconfigurable antenna (RA)-enhanced ISAC systems. We distinguish transceiver-side (TSc-side) and environment-side (Env-side) RA deployments and identify five fundamental EM reconfiguration dimensions: position, orientation, radiation pattern, polarization, and frequency response. Building on this framework, we examine how these dimensions customize communication channels, actively control target information mapping for sensing, and reshape the interplay between S&C, particularly by improving compatibility between S&C requirements under shared resources. Two case studies illustrate how TSc-side and Env-side EM reconfiguration can improve spatial selectivity and the achievable S&C performance tradeoff. Finally, we discuss several promising directions for advancing RA-enhanced ISAC systems, including fundamental performance limits, low-overhead black-box optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled semantic ISAC.

Systems and Control.title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
Systems and Control.summary: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.

Systems and Control.title: Translate, then decide: asymptotic optimality of latent-space control in bistable systems
Systems and Control.summary: This paper asks whether an optimal decision can be separated from the physical dynamics on which it acts. It studies this question through minimum-energy barrier crossing in scalar bistable systems. It characterizes the finite-horizon optimal feedback and shows that, as the horizon grows, it converges to a law that doubles and reverses the drift while it opposes crossing, and switches off once the barrier is passed. In physical coordinates, this law inherits the plant's nonlinearity, entangling decision and dynamics. We show that a plant-specific translation of state, input, and time maps every double well in the considered class to the same unit-rate linear world model, allowing a downstream decision stage to use a single plant-independent control primitive. This separation generally loses optimality at finite horizons because the translation does not preserve the physical control energy. Nevertheless, we prove that the excess physical energy of the layered controller vanishes as the horizon grows and that its limiting feedback reproduces the asymptotic optimum exactly. Thus, translation and optimization generally do not commute at a finite horizon, but commute in the asymptotic limit.

Systems and Control.title: A Game-Theoretic Decision Framework for Optimal Selection of Coordination Detection Methods in Multi-UAV Fleet Operations
Systems and Control.summary: Detecting coordination among unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) fleets operating in shared airspace and identifying the route-lead aircraft whose navigation decisions govern fleet behavior presents a fundamental speed--accuracy trade-off: fast methods enable real-time traffic management but sacrifice detection fidelity, while accurate methods may exceed the time budget for actionable airspace deconfliction. This paper presents a game-theoretic decision framework that resolves this trade-off by formulating method selection as a two-player zero-sum game between a Monitor (selecting computational methods and parameters) and Nature (selecting the unknown traffic scenario). We construct an end-to-end pipeline from trajectory surveillance data through eight candidate detection algorithms, a Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis characterizing their stochastic performance, and finally a multi-objective optimization layer that identifies Pareto-optimal method portfolios. The minimax solution provides a robust mixed strategy with a probability distribution over methods that guarantees worst-case performance regardless of scenario uncertainty. Experimental evaluation across 200 randomized configurations spanning 5--50 aircraft demonstrates that the framework recommends distinct method portfolios depending on operational priority: Koopman Phase dominates balanced (70.6%) and speed-priority (79.7%) profiles, while CRQA emerges as primary (47.4%) when route-lead identification is prioritized. The framework achieves a guaranteed game value of 0.29--0.53 (normalized utility) across all tested preference profiles, providing the first principled, scenario-adaptive methodology for computational method selection in UTM fleet monitoring operations.

Systems and Control.title: Decentralized Impedance Specifications for Grid-Connected Converters: a Sequence-Domain Gershgorin Method, and a Frequency-Wise Framework for Combining Different Criteria
Systems and Control.summary: In complex grid scenarios, with many power electronics (PE) converters connected, having specifications for converters can ease the design process. A practical approach is to impose the specifications on the converter's small-signal impedance in the frequency domain. This is advantageous since impedance is a physical property that can be measured. This paper focuses on providing decentralized impedance specifications for each converter connected to an ac bus. With decentralized specifications, each converter has its own specifications, which are independent of other converters' impedance. This enables a competitive multi-vendor environment while guaranteeing system stability. Existing methods of imposing decentralized specifications, based on the small-gain, passivity and Gershgorin theorems, are formulated within a common frequency-domain framework. Building on this, two new solutions that reduce the conservativeness of the specifications are proposed. First, Gershgorin-based decentralized specifications are formulated in the modified sequence domain. Second, a framework for combining different specification types across frequency ranges is developed and mathematically proven. The methods are compared on examples covering sub-synchronous and harmonic-range interactions of grid-following converters, grid-forming converters, and a mixed grid-forming/grid-following system, using analytical models, black-box impedance measurements, and time-domain responses obtained from simulations and an experimental setup.

Systems and Control.title: Model Predictive Control of Heating Systems via Koopman-Operator Bilinearization
Systems and Control.summary: Hydronic heat emitters are widely used in buildings, but their control is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics, arising from both the heat transfer in each emitter and the hydraulic coupling among those that share a circulating pump. These nonlinearities are often simplified or neglected in the literature. In this paper, we use Koopman theory to make the resulting model more tractable for control. In particular, we propose an input reparameterization and construct an infinite-dimensional set of observables that yields an exact bilinear representation of the system in the chosen lifted space. We then show that truncating the infinite-dimensional representation leads to bounded approximation errors that decrease as the truncation order increases, as well as bounded trajectory deviations over a finite horizon. The resulting bilinear model is incorporated into a model predictive control (MPC) framework to provide thermal comfort in multi-zone buildings while reducing energy use. Using a numerical case study of a five-story building with 20 zones, we show that the proposed Koopman-based MPC achieves a realized performance cost close to that of nonlinear MPC with faster solve times, and outperforms MPC formulations based on time-invariant and time-varying linearizations.

Systems and Control.title: Barrier-State-Based Safe Navigation in Complex Environments Using Look-Ahead Safety Corridors
Systems and Control.summary: Safe navigation in cluttered environments requires a safety representation that captures the available motion space along the planned path. A single local safe region may restrict progress through narrow passages and continuous turns. This paper presents a planning-guided look-ahead safety corridor framework for barrier-state-based navigation. Local safe convex polytopes are constructed around collision-free seeds along the forward reference path. Their facet constraints are combined using softmin, and the local functions are fused using softmax with entropy-based adaptive compensation. The resulting safe set remains within the union of the local polytopes while reducing the shrinkage caused by fixed compensation. A Poisson boundary-value problem then defines a differentiable interior safety field while preserving the prescribed corridor boundary. This field is embedded into the robot dynamics through one geometric barrier state. We establish sufficient conditions for corridor invariance based on barrier-state boundedness and active-corridor validity. Navigation simulations cover cluttered layouts, narrow passages, and moving obstacles. A differential-drive ground vehicle further demonstrates navigation through narrow passages and among obstacles absent from the prior map.

Systems and Control.title: A Hetero-functional Graph State Estimator for Watershed Systems: Application to the Chesapeake Bay
Systems and Control.summary: Regional watersheds are systems of systems in which hydrology, land use, and governance interact. Nutrient models such as the Chesapeake Assessment Scenario Tool (CAST) route nutrients from land to the estuary through lumped delivery factors, so the river network that connects sources to the estuary is not represented explicitly. This paper develops a region-independent watershed reference architecture in Hetero-functional Graph Theory (HFGT) and adapts the Weighted Least Squares Error Hetero-functional Graph State Estimator to estimate nutrient flows in that network from uncertain data. The framework is applied to the Chesapeake Bay watershed. A mass-conserving network of land segments, outlet points, and river reaches is built from public geospatial data. CAST applied loads, land-segment edge-of-river loads, and river-to-bay delivery factors enter the estimator as measurements, each with its own error term. CAST-reported loads delivered to the Bay are withheld from estimation and used only to test the estimated delivery. The estimator reproduces the applied loads (R^2=1.00) and the land-segment edge-of-river loads (R^2=0.997) and under-predicts delivery to the Bay by 8.0% for nitrogen and 5.7% for phosphorus. The gap is traced to CAST delivery factors that imply in-river gains, which a mass-conserving network cannot represent, and to land segments whose edge-of-river loads exceed their applied loads. The framework provides a common systems representation for coupling watershed models with infrastructure, economic, and governance models.

Systems and Control.title: A System-of-Systems Convergence Paradigm for Societal Challenges of the Anthropocene
Systems and Control.summary: Climate, water, food, energy and governance challenges are interdependent, yet the tools used to study and manage them remain divided by discipline and sector. Coupling sectoral models pair by pair cannot keep pace with the cross-sector and institutional interactions that drive global environmental change. In this Perspective we argue that convergence requires a shared system ontology that preserves meaning as knowledge moves from observation to computation and back to decision-making. Building on a meta-cognition map of scientific knowledge generation, we propose six design criteria for convergent system-of-systems approaches and assess four candidate methods against them, identifying model-based systems engineering paired with hetero-functional graph theory as a candidate "convergence spine". We illustrate the paradigm in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed, where a single ontology links nutrient-flow estimation, institutional analysis of restoration governance, team science and graduate education, and we distinguish what has been implemented from what remains future work. We close with implications for how global environmental change research is organized, funded and taught.

Systems and Control.title: Data-Driven Stochastic LQR Control with Probabilistic Guarantees and Uncertainty Refinement
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a probabilistic framework for the direct, data-driven synthesis of the stochastic linear- quadratic output-feedback control for linear systems sub- ject to process and measurement noise. Using delayed input-output measurements, we derive a lifted parameter- ization together with an equivalent lifted linear quadratic cost, enabling controller synthesis without explicitly identi- fying the lifted dynamics. Two complementary closed-loop formulations, based on trajectory and covariance represen- tations, are then developed, whose uncertainties depend only on the realized but unknown lifted noise. We char- acterize the relative performance of the two formulations in finite-data regimes. High-probability uncertainty bounds are developed for realized noises, leading to a convex optimization solution to the problem, whose feasibility cer- tifies probabilistic mean-square stability (p-MSS) and per- formance guarantees. To reduce conservatism, Gaussian zonotopes are used to refine uncertainty sets by elimi- nating noise realizations inconsistent with measured data, and a novel intersection rule enables the consistent fusion of data-driven and physics-informed information. These components are integrated into an adaptive framework that unifies indirect (identification-based) and direct (control- oriented) data-driven linear-quadratic output-feedback con- trol. Unlike existing direct data-driven LQR methods that verify stability a posteriori, our by-construction approach achieves robust stability alongside reduced conservatism and superior performance. Simulation results show that the proposed controller approaches the ideal optimal solution while outperforming existing data-driven methods under noisy measurements.

Systems and Control.title: An Introduction to Model-Based Systems Engineering and Hetero-functional Graph Theory for Hydrological Systems of Systems
Systems and Control.summary: This introductory overview describes a unified modeling framework for representing interconnected environmental systems using Model-Based Systems Engineering and Hetero-functional Graph Theory. Existing environmental models encode rich structural and process-level information, yet much of this knowledge remains implicit within domain-specific formulations. This paper demonstrates how such information can be formalized into a consistent ontology that explicitly represents system structure, function, and interconnections. Using illustrative hydrological examples, the tutorial illustrates how conventional process models can be translated into a scalable system-of-systems representation. Agricultural nitrogen applied to land is represented explicitly as the point at which human decisions enter the hydrological system, illustrating how models of human systems can be coupled to hydrological models within the same representation. These examples highlight how embedded relationships in existing models can be made explicit and computationally tractable. Using simplified examples, the overview provides a foundation for integrating heterogeneous models across environmental and engineered domains. More broadly, this work offers a step-by-step introduction to a generalizable modeling framework for complex systems.

Systems and Control.title: Dexterous In-Hand Object Pose Reaching with Learned Safety Filters
Systems and Control.summary: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals. We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum. With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust. On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops. In 13.3 hours of real-robot evaluation over 4,800 unseen goals across 4 objects and diverse wrist orientations, the state-based policy reaches 95.2% of goals within 2 cm and 0.4 rad, and the filter cuts its drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals. The policies can also spin a lightbulb held in an arbitrary pose, reach out-of-distribution goals, withstand fast arm motion and perturbations, and, needing only a wrist camera, serve as portable skills such as screwing in a lightbulb. We release the full recipe as a platform for studying performance, reliability, and safety in high-dimensional dexterous systems. Videos and more are available at https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/.
Systems and Control.comment: 26 pages, 30 figures, 14 tables. Project page: https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/

Systems and Control.title: Iterative Methods for Solving Feedback-Type Linear Equations under Small Phase Condition
Systems and Control.summary: This paper investigates iterative methods for solving feedback-type linear equations under small phase condition. We first develop an iterative solution scheme for linear equations with sectorial (semi-sectorial) matrices, i.e., matrices whose numerical ranges are contained in an open (closed) half complex plane. Exploiting the geometric properties of the numerical range, we introduce the notion of numerical-radius contraction as a convergence criterion. Such a scheme, with some extra effort, leads to an iterative method for the feedback-type equations under small phase condition, whose convergence condition is characterized in terms of phase information. This complements classical iterative methods for feedback-type equations based on the small gain condition. A case study on large-scale power networks is presented to illustrate the computational efficiency of the proposed method.

Systems and Control.title: Quantile Propagation Planning for Budgeted Tail-Risk Evaluation
